summary: PARTIAL stands. The server half is fixed by #710 (60633eff3). SourceControlDiscovery, ProviderMaintenanceRunner and ContextHandoffInspection are now process-wide in RuntimeServicesLive. Per-connection builds on direct /ws and relay reuse them through the forked CurrentMemoMap; I traced this through effect 4.0.2's MemoMapImpl parent fallthrough, HttpRouter.serve and HubConnectorDeferred. Every leaf of the leftover provisions in ws.ts is also in the server graph. discoverSourceControl serves the 2-minute TTL cache when cached:true is sent. The client half is not done. WsRpcGroup is still monolithic, the main WsTransport uses the merged app+device group, and agentControl.ts, device.ts, changeRequestReview.ts and relay.ts are still in the 895 KB boot chunk, while hostedIdentity, nativeE2ee, nativeHandoff and computer have left it. The auditor's remaining-work plan is wrong, though. The agent-control RPC surface is not cold: subscribeProposals starts at shell mount for every connected environment, and its stream schema needs the whole action-plan part of agentControl.ts, which imports device.ts. So splitting the agent-control or device RPC groups would save almost nothing. The cheap, real remaining win is different: about 38 KB of raw source of server-only MCP tool schemas inside agentControl.ts ship in the client boot chunk, because top-level Schema calls are not tree-shaken within a module.

evidence.note: SourceControlDiscovery.layer, ProviderMaintenanceRunner.layer and ContextHandoffInspectionLive are in RuntimeServicesLive (process-wide). ChatAttachmentUploadsLive is in the runtime base at server.ts:575. All leaves of the ws.ts provisions (VcsDriverRegistry, VcsProjectConfig, GitVcsDriver, ForgejoApi, SourceControlProviderRegistry, ServerSecretStoreLive, AtlassianConnectionRepositoryLive, SqlitePersistenceLayerLive, ContextHandoffRepositoryLive, VcsProcess) are the same objects in server.ts:330-511 and :838, so they hit the memo too.

Only leaf layers (fromBuildMemo) memoize, and lookup falls through to the parent memo map. buildWithMemoMap puts CurrentMemoMap into both the build fiber and the output context. provideWith rebuilds the composed chains per connection, but each leaf resolves to the process-wide instance.
HttpRouter.serve builds routes with a fork of the launch memo map, so the /ws handler's Effect.provide (ws.ts:87-89) forks again and falls through to the runtime memo map.
The relay path captures the build context (including CurrentMemoMap), and HubConnectorLive.ts:346 runs relay RPC sessions with it, so HubConnectorLive.ts:583-589 also reuses the shared instances.

input.cached === true selects discover (TTL Cache, SourceControlDiscovery.ts:146-161, 2 min TTL); otherwise refresh. Background callers send cached:true (packages/client-runtime/src/sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts:181, apps/web/src/lib/sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts). Only explicit refreshes (SourceControlSettings, CommandPalette) re-probe.
WsDeviceRpcGroup and the monolithic WsRpcGroup (agentControl :2781-2797, automationCentre, change request review :2685) live in one module. WsHostedRpcGroup = WsRpcGroup.merge(WsDeviceRpcGroup).

Module-level RpcClient.make for the app, device and merged hosted groups. The main WsTransport uses the merged group (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:610-618), and connection/atomRpcClient.ts:26 uses WsRpcGroup. The file wsTransport.ts still exists; only the separate wsTransport-* chunk is gone, merged into boot.

Built 5 min after HEAD. A literal probe across contracts modules shows these in boot: orchestration, agentControl (216/217), rpc, providerRuntime, settings, device (58/67), relay (54/54), changeRequestReview (19/19). Absent: computer (4/57), hostedIdentity (2/88), nativeE2ee (3/29), nativeHandoff (1/25), computerBrowser (0/35), localIntroduction and desktopNativeNodeClaim (0). These modules are re-exported from the barrel (packages/contracts/src/index.ts:7-8,58-63) and sideEffects:false, which proves the bundler drops unused modules but keeps every top-level Schema of any module it includes.

AutomationsEntry calls useWaitingAutomationRuns() → useAutomationProposalSync(all connected envs) (apps/web/src/components/automations/useWaitingAutomationRuns.ts:17-23). RootAppShell.tsx:100 also mounts MissedAutomationRunsNotice (useAutomationProposalSync at :243). agentControl.subscribeProposals is therefore attempted at shell mount for every connected environment (useAutomationProposalSync.ts:26-60), so the agent-control RPC group is hot, not cold.

AgentControlProposalStreamEvent → AgentControlProposal → AgentControlActionPlan covers agentControl.ts:1-1065 (~46 KB source), including the simulator-plan section that imports device.ts values (agentControl.ts:60-71). A lazy agent-control or device RPC client would be loaded immediately after boot anyway.

This range holds the internal provider-session MCP surface, the tool inputs, the tool results and the external stdio MCP tool catalog: 94 exports, about 38 KB of raw source. It has zero importers in apps/web, apps/mobile, packages/client-runtime or packages/shared, and nothing in the client-reachable ranges of agentControl.ts or in other contracts modules references it (only a comment in agentControlDelegation.ts:13). Even so, all of its literals (56/56, 21/21, 35/35 and the long description strings) are in the boot chunk. Server consumers (~20 files under apps/server/src/agentControl, provider/ProviderDriver.ts, server.ts) import via the @ryco/contracts barrel. The Hub does not import them.

remaining: Client side only; the server half is done. (1) Main concrete remaining cost: packages/contracts/src/agentControl.ts:1362-2164 (internal provider-session MCP surface, tool inputs, tool results) and :2390-end (external stdio MCP tool catalog) are server-only, about 38 KB of raw source and roughly 15-25 KB minified, yet they are evaluated in the web boot chunk. agentControl.ts is a hot module, imported by the RPC group, by wsRpcClient.ts:13 and by state/agentControl, and Schema declarations are not tree-shaken within a module. (2) Cold RPC payloads are still evaluated at boot because WsRpcGroup and WsDeviceRpcGroup share rpc.ts (rpc.ts:2247,2392,2826) and the main transport uses the merged group (wsTransport.ts:617). Truly cold parts: agent-control integration/MCP-installation admin schemas (agentControl.ts:2164-2390, ~10 KB source), device control-plane payloads (device.ts:311-end, ~23 KB source; device.ts:1-311 stays hot via agentControl.ts:60-71), and changeRequestReview.ts (~18 KB source). relay.ts is pulled in by non-RPC importers. The auditor's main proposal, splitting the agent-control RPCs into a lazy group, would gain almost nothing: subscribeProposals runs at shell mount (SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:196, RootAppShell.tsx:100) and needs agentControl.ts:1-1065 plus device.ts:1-311.
fixDefects: No functional defect in the server fix. Minor: no test asserts that per-connection and relay RPC layers resolve to the process-wide SourceControlDiscovery, ProviderMaintenanceRunner and ContextHandoffInspection instances. The reuse depends on the request or relay fiber still carrying CurrentMemoMap. If that were lost, the fallback provisions in ws.ts:34-60 would silently rebuild those services, and their caches, per connection. The cached flag is opt-in, so older clients still re-probe on every call. That is acceptable, because explicit refresh must bypass the cache.
implementationSketch: Step A (worth doing, effort S): move the server-only Agent Control MCP schemas out of agentControl.ts. Create packages/contracts/src/agentControlMcp.ts and move agentControl.ts:1362-2164 and :2390-end into it, importing the base identifiers and schemas it needs from ./agentControl.ts (the dependency goes one way only, since nothing client-reachable references the moved code). Add `export * from "./agentControlMcp.ts"` to packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Server code imports these names via the @ryco/contracts barrel, so almost no server import changes are needed; check apps/server/src/agentControl/** and provider/ProviderDriver.ts with typecheck. Optionally add an `./agent-control-mcp` subpath to packages/contracts/package.json. Fix packages/contracts/src/agentControl.test.ts and projectChats.test.ts imports if they reference the moved names via ./agentControl.ts. Verify: run `bun run build --filter=@ryco/web`, then probe apps/web/dist/assets/boot-*.js for distinctive moved literals (e.g. ryco_create_task, the stdio catalog tool descriptions, and the internal-MCP description strings). They should be absent, and the boot chunk should shrink by about 15-25 KB minified. Run focused vitest for packages/contracts and apps/server/src/agentControl, plus bun typecheck. Optional guard: a small vitest that bundles or imports the client entry graph and asserts agentControlMcp.ts is unreachable. Step B (optional, low value, effort M): to also defer the cold RPC payloads, split rpc.ts into feature group modules: WsDeviceRpcGroup in its own module, plus the agent-control integration/MCP-installation admin RPCs and the changeRequestReview RPC. Split device.ts at ~line 311 into hot identifiers/descriptor/availability and cold control-plane payloads. Make the main WsTransport (wsTransport.ts:617) use WsRpcGroup without device. Create secondary RpcClients lazily (dynamic import of the group module) over the same socket protocol; Effect 4's socket protocol already multiplexes clientIds (effect/src/rpc/RpcClient.ts:1249-1254). This needs RpcTransport to expose its protocol and scope for extra clients and to keep admission, latency tracking and reconnect semantics per request. The server keeps serving the merged group on /ws (ws.ts:79), so the wire protocol does not change. Test with the browser suite for device and integrations settings plus wsTransport unit tests. Do not split the agent-control proposal RPCs: they are hot.
decisionReason: Step A only moves schema declarations between contracts modules. Wire format, RPC tags, auth, E2EE and Hub protocol are unchanged, and the Hub does not import the moved names. Step B also keeps the wire API (the server still serves the merged group) and is optional.
correction: The auditor's PARTIAL classification and server-side analysis are correct. Their remaining-work plan is wrong in two ways. First, it treats the agent-control RPCs as cold and proposes a lazy agent-control group plus making agentControl.ts unreachable from boot, estimating 30-35 KiB. In fact subscribeProposals is started at shell mount for every connected environment (SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:196 → useWaitingAutomationRuns → useAutomationProposalSync, and RootAppShell.tsx:100 → MissedAutomationRunsNotice), and its schema needs agentControl.ts:1-1065, which imports device.ts. So neither the agent-control nor the device group split saves much, and agentControl.ts cannot leave the startup path. Second, they missed the real cheap win: about 38 KB of raw source of server-only MCP tool schemas (agentControl.ts:1362-2164, 2390-end) that ship in the client boot chunk only because they share a module with client-used schemas. Minor: wsTransport.ts the file still exists (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts); only the separate chunk is gone.
